decisions.reason: As a sensor module tightly aligned with the firm's established modular hardware, firmware, and API capabilities, it is the kind of product the firm can readily improve and learn from commercially.
Because it directly replaces an earlier voltage-measurement product, it builds on strong prior knowledge and an existing user need, making continuation highly likely.
The MQTT proxy fits the firm's connectivity and software-binding strengths, though as a software-side complement it is somewhat easier to discontinue if adoption proves weaker than expected.
A CAN bus interface extends the platform into automation and embedded communication markets that are close to the firm's core technical base and customer applications.
A carbon dioxide sensor module fits squarely within the firm's sensing portfolio, where its existing electronics, firmware, and documentation capabilities support further refinement.

The touch panel accessory is more peripheral to the firm's core sensing and control modules, so it faces a higher discontinuation risk, but it still complements the platform enough to justify staying on the market for now.
